Analysis 2 is a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked result (whole-brain model fit and inference; Monte Carlo cluster correction; reported peaks/Table T2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected evidence. Although an ROI analysis is also reported (Analysis 0), it is not the sole voxelwise result. Participant and task details are provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI, only connectivity, only between-group contrasts, non-empirical) are met.

Study uses individualized guided-imagery scripts (stress, cue, neutral) rather than a clear visual cue component, so it fails inclusion criterion I3. The reported statistical result is a three-way omnibus interaction (between-group contrast) and does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast needed by I4. The study does report whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinate peaks (satisfying I5 and I6) and reports participant characteristics (I7). Because only between-group/interaction results are presented without an accompanying within-subject cue>control contrast, exclusion criterion E5 is met. Inclusion met: I5, I6, I7. Inclusion not met: I3, I4. Exclusion met: E5.

The NeuroStore record reports only resting-state nodal-degree group comparisons (patients vs controls) with a fixation/rest task and no task-based cue paradigm. No within-participant drug-cues > control-stimulus contrast is reported. Therefore the paper does not provide a task-evoked, cue-reactivity voxelwise result. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state analyses without qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no clear visual drug cue paradigm reported), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast), I5 (no task-evoked group-level voxelwise result). Full text appears complete in the record: no access issues were indicated.

The NeuroStore record reports an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual opioid-related images and an explicit within-subject drug>neutral contrast. Analyses were voxelwise, fit over the whole brain with whole-brain inference (TFCE, cluster-level) and reported peak coordinates (tables). These details satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (visual cues), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain result), and I6 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes within-participant cue>control). Full text appears available via the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The paper reports only an interaction/between-group contrast (Sham vs Real acupuncture interaction across Session and Cue) rather than a within-participant smoking > neutral (cue>control) contrast. Although the study meets inclusion for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual smoking cues (I3), reports whole-brain voxelwise results (I5) and allows reporting of peaks/tables (I6), it does not present a qualifying within-subject drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast. This satisfies exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group/interaction reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study of 41 recently detoxified alcohol-dependent subjects used visual alcohol-related and neutral images (12 alcohol blocks, 9 neutral blocks) and reported whole-brain group-level voxelwise results for the within-subject alcohol>neutral contrast (one-sample t-test) with peak coordinates (Table). It also reports a cross-subject regression linking acylated ghrelin to alcohol cue activation (whole-brain multiple regression). These satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-participant cue>control contrast, and at least one whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result (coordinate tables acceptable). Participant demographics and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject cue>control contrast, empirical human fMRI data).

The study examines neural responses to visual smoking cues (cigarette image) and monetary cues within a within-participant, crossover design. NeuroStore extraction reports event-related task contrasts (reward type, condition) and a within-group omnibus contrast, with model terms including reward type, indicating within-participant comparisons of cue types. The reported analysis used voxelwise inference restricted to anatomically defined regions (ROI) with cluster-level correction (3dClusterSim) and reported peak coordinates in ventral/dorsal striatum and mPFC, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected results. Participant demographics (age/sex) and stimuli are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not report a within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast (I4 not met). The NeuroStore extract shows multiple reported results that are between-group contrasts or interactions (object category × group, modality × group, main effects between smokers and nonsmokers) and modality comparisons (visual>haptic, haptic>visual). The only within-group voxelwise result relates to within-smoker correlations between the HS–VS contrast and FTND, which is a covariate association and not a smoking-cues > control contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual smoking cues present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (results reported as peaks/tables), I7 (participant demographics reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study investigates smoking-related cue reactivity using visual stimuli (images) in adolescent light smokers and reports a within-subject contrast (smoking > neutral). Analysis 0 is a group-level second-level random-effects GLM with model fit and inference across the whole brain and reports peak coordinates (Table), satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise whole-brain result. Results are reported in tables, acceptable per I6. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not provided but are not mandatory. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, only-connectivity, or only between-group contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets core inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to alcohol-related visual stimuli (15 alcohol pictures vs neutral/scrambled), satisfying visual cue requirement. It includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol-associated versus control pictures (reported as within-group interaction analyses comparing before vs after amisulpride, indicating that first-level alcohol>control contrasts were used), and group-level voxelwise results were estimated over the whole brain and reported as thresholded voxelwise peaks/tables. Coordinates/peaks are reported in tables. Participant demographics and cue type are provided. MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not listed in this extract but missing methodological details do not preclude inclusion per criteria. Therefore I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual smoking-related images (ISIS/IAPS) in chronic cigarette smokers and includes a within-subject SMOKING > NEUTRAL contrast (Analysis 1). A group-level voxelwise result is reported with small-volume correction (FDR SVC, p<0.05) and coordinate peaks (Table t2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC task-evoked voxelwise evidence. Connectivity (PPI) analyses are present but do not preclude inclusion because a qualifying task-evoked contrast is reported. Participant demographics and cue type are provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports cue-reactivity to cigarette and alcohol using visual stimuli and within-participant drug>control contrasts, but all reported analyses are ROI-based (model fit over: region of interest; thresholding: region-level; one-sample t-tests on averaged ROI data). No group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result).

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue reactivity using visual smoking images; reports within-participant Smoking > Neutral contrasts for both groups; and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results with cluster-corrected inference and reported peak coordinates (tables). The task and stimuli are visual (International Smoking Image Series). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-participant contrasts). Sufficient methodological reporting is present to qualify under I6. Therefore the study should be included.

This fMRI study used visual heroin-related cues (Cue Reactivity Task) and reports within-subject contrasts of heroin cues > neutral cues in opioid-dependent participants (Analysis 18823721_analysis_0), satisfying the required drug-cue > control contrast. At least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result is reported with whole-brain inference and voxelwise FDR thresholding (Analysis 0), meeting the whole-brain/small-volume requirement. The paper reports participant age/sex and cue type; missing MRI field strength is allowable per criteria. Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study directly addresses fMRI cue-reactivity to smoking (a drug reward) and includes visual stimuli (pictures) and multisensory conditions. It reports within-participant contrasts Smoke>Neutral (several analyses) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FLAME1, whole-brain inference, cluster-corrected thresholds) with peak coordinate tables. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or between-group-only, and is empirical).

The study used visual cannabis cues and reports whole-brain voxelwise task results (Analyses 5 and 6) and multiple seed-based gPPI connectivity results. However, all reported task-based contrasts appear to be between-group interaction contrasts (patient vs control for cue>neutral) rather than a reported within-participant cue>control (cue>neutral) contrast for either group alone. Exclusion reason: E5 (study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual drug cue reactivity), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no explicit within-participant drug cues>control stimuli contrast reported). fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol images (30 alcohol images vs neutral/IAPS and scrambled controls) with an event-related cue-reactivity task. The second-level model includes a cue-type term and reports whole-brain voxelwise inference (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain) with cluster-level FWE correction (AFNI 3dClustSim) and reported peak coordinates (Table tab2) in multiple regions (insula, thalamus, pallidum, etc.). These constitute group-level voxelwise task-evoked results for drug (alcohol) cues versus control stimuli, reported as coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue details are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group without within-participant cue>control) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

The study reports a within-participant, drug-cue (cocaine film) > control contrast (Analysis 11058476_analysis_0) using BOLD fMRI during visual (film) stimulus presentation. That analysis is a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain one-sample t-test with voxelwise thresholding and cluster reporting (Table 2, 19 peaks), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Visual cue component, within-subject contrast, whole-brain voxelwise reporting, and coordinate-table reporting are all present. Participant age/sex are reported; missing preprocessing/field-strength details do not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, within-participant contrast is present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

The study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol images (beer, wine, spirits) versus neutral visual stimuli and includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral). Analyses were conducted and reported as whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (model fit and inference over the whole brain) with reported peak coordinates/tables. Participant demographics and task details are provided. Therefore it satisfies I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (coordinates/tables reported), and I7 (participant/task details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrast).

The abstract reports a cue-reactivity fMRI task with cocaine cues and appetitive control stimuli, including within-participant contrasts (cocaine cues relative to appetitive stimuli) and group-level voxelwise activation findings (increased activation in DLPFC, occipital cortex; OFC for cocaine vs appetitive stimuli; craving-related activity in PCC). These constitute a task-evoked voxelwise result (whole-brain/small-volume) qualifying under the meta-analysis. Although NeuroStore’s extracted analyses emphasize resting-state seed-based connectivity, the abstract explicitly reports task-evoked cue>control results. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (drug cue-reactivity with visual cue component implied by cue-reactivity task), I4 (within-participant cue vs control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked result), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats) are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Confidence downgraded to moderate because the extract lacks tabulated task-contrast coordinates in the provided analyses list, so the presence of voxelwise task results is inferred from the abstract rather than extracted tables.

This fMRI study used clear visual cues (e-cigarette videos vs electronic toothbrush videos) and included within-subject contrasts. NeuroStore lists a within-group e-cigarette>neutral contrast (pre-vaping; ROI) and, importantly, a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result for a main effect of cue (omnibus, within-group) with cluster-level inference and reported peaks/tables. Thus the paper provides a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked group result (satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected evidence) and reports coordinate peaks (acceptable per I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported, but MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not given (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This study matches the meta-analysis objective and meets required inclusion criteria: it uses visual drug-related cues (nine drug-related film clips) and includes a within-participant contrast Drug movies > Neutral movies. The analysis is a group-level voxelwise whole-brain GLM with FWE correction and reported peak coordinates (Table tbl0010), satisfying the ‘whole-brain or small-volume-corrected’ requirement; results are reported as coordinates per inclusion guidance. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported in the NeuroStore record (preferred reporting per I7), but missing these details does not preclude inclusion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures vs houses), satisfying the review topic. It reports a within-participant contrast of alcohol>neutral (Analysis 26295336_analysis_0 and related contrasts) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain inference (analyses 0,1,2,6) and reported coordinate peaks/tables. Results are available in tables/peaks, and participant age/sex and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol vs nonalcoholic-beverage photographs and includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol > beverage). The analysis was a group-level voxelwise whole-brain GLM (model fit over whole brain) with reported peaks (table of coordinates) and statistical thresholding, satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise task-evoked result. Participant demographics and MRI field strength (3.0-T) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes the required within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This study examines alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol and soft-drink images (meets I3). It reports a within-participant alcohol>soft drink contrast at group-level (Analysis 25526597_analysis_0 and within-group analyses) satisfying I4. Model fitting was performed over the whole brain and inferences used voxel-level FWE small-volume correction (SVC), i.e. voxelwise SVC results are reported (meets I5 and I6 via reported peaks/coordinates). Participant age/sex and cue details are reported; missing MRI field-strength/software is a non-excluding omission (I7). The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears available in the record.

The study reports within-subject cue-reactivity contrasts (Smoking > Food) using visual stimuli (smoking and food videos). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results were estimated and inference was performed over the whole brain (peaks reported in tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence. Coordinate tables and thresholding approach are provided. Participant demographics and preprocessing/software details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only).

This fMRI study examines alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol pictures and neutral IAPS images (meets I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol>neutral (analysis 4: ‘alcohol > neutral’, group-level one-sample t test with reported peaks), satisfying the required cue>control within-subject contrast (I4). Group-level voxelwise results are reported both as whole-brain results (analysis 4, reported peaks/table) and as small-volume-corrected ROI results (analyses 0 and 1), fulfilling I5. Results are presented in tables of coordinates (I6). Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported; MRI field strength is not listed but missing details are allowable per I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject cue>control). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports only seed-based connectivity analyses (wavelet transform coherence between right amygdala and whole brain) during attempted inhibition of cue-induced craving while viewing a cocaine-related video. The meta-analysis requires a within-participant cue>control (or natural reward>control) voxelwise task-evoked contrast (whole-brain or SVC). No within-participant drug-cues>control contrast or task-evoked activation map is reported here; instead the reported results are connectivity (between-group/parametric modulation) peaks. Therefore this study cannot contribute qualifying task-evoked voxelwise activation data.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking images (60 full-color smoking pictures) and an event-related design, reporting group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (model fit over: whole brain) for within-participant contrasts of smoke > control. Peak coordinates are reported in tables for multiple smoke>control analyses (including cross-subject regressions with FTND, craving, negative affect, and sex). These features satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (visual cues), I4 (within-participant drug cue > control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (coordinates reported in tables). Participant demographics and task details are provided (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria. I3: The task uses visual smoking and nonsmoking control photographs (visual cue component). I4: The abstract and reported analyses indicate within-participant cue contrasts comparing smoking vs control cues, and the authors report alcohol-enhanced ventral striatum responses to smoking compared with control cues. I5: Group-level voxelwise results were reported with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (FDR-corrected and voxelwise uncorrected contrasts). I6: Results are reported in tables of peaks (reported peaks listed) and thresholding details are provided. No exclusion criteria apply: the study reports voxelwise task-evoked results (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), and includes within-participant cue contrasts. Participant and task details are provided. Full text is available in the provided record.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (images of marzipan objects). It includes a within-participant CS+>CS- contrast (analysis 32553642_analysis_2) tested at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (MNI). Participant demographics and task details are reported. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

The NeuroStore record reports only a between-group interaction contrast (Placebo > 30 mg/day baclofen) tested at the whole-brain level; no within-participant drug-cue > control (alcohol cues > neutral) contrast is reported. Exclusion E5 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI alcohol cue reactivity with clear visual picture stimuli), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result reported), I6 (peaks/coordinates reported in table), I7 (participant age/sex and other sample details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast available in the document). Thus the study must be excluded under E5.

Excluded per E5: the paper reports only between-group interactions (patients vs. controls; relapsers vs. controls; abstainers vs. controls) for alcohol-cue > neutral contrasts and does not present an accompanying within-participant drug-cue > control contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual alcohol cues used), I5 (at least one group-level voxelwise result reported — analysis_1 whole-brain corrected), I6 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast reported). Full text is available in this record; exclusion is based on the analyses reported.

This study examines fMRI smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral pictures) and reports ROI-based activation measures used in cross-subject Cox regressions predicting lapse. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual drug cue reactivity) and I4 (within-participant cue task yielding condition-specific activation used in analysis). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical result is reported; NeuroStore extraction indicates model fit and thresholding were restricted to a priori ROIs. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (only ROI analyses reported with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Full text is available from the record (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis because it lacks qualifying voxelwise results required by I5.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual grayscale smoking cues (I3). It reports a within-subject contrast of CUE>neutral (within-participant cue>control) (I4). The contrast was modeled and tested at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; voxelwise correction) satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result (I5). NeuroStore record provides coordinate peaks and details consistent with reporting of voxelwise results (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study assesses visual smoking-related cue-reactivity (smoking-related pictures vs neutral) using fMRI, reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with cluster-corrected thresholding and coordinate peaks, and includes a within-subject analysis testing Smoke>Neutral across timepoints (a within-group interaction), which provides task-evoked voxelwise evidence suitable for meta-analysis of cue>control effects. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting/connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts without any within-participant cue>control contrast) are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using clear visual heroin-related cues (images of injection, preparation, paraphernalia) (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of heroin-related cues > neutral cues (multiple within-group analyses) (I4). Voxelwise, group-level task-evoked results were reported over the whole brain with voxelwise inference and FDR correction and peaks reported in tables of coordinates (I5,I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not extracted but missing details do not preclude inclusion (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-participant contrasts).

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli (20 pictures per cue category), satisfying I3. It reports within-subject contrasts of MJ cues > non-MJ cues (several analyses), satisfying I4. Results are reported as voxelwise peaks/coordinate tables with inference restricted to anatomically defined ROIs and cluster correction using AFNI 3dClustSim (p<0.005, cluster extent), which constitutes small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, satisfying I5 and I6. Participant demographics and cue details are reported, satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply: although analyses were ROI-restricted, they include small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (so E3 does not apply). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual images (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie > low-calorie food images (I4). Importantly, it includes a whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result (Analysis 30991304_analysis_1: whole-brain high>low contrast with reported peaks), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result (I5). Results are reported as peak tables/analyses (I6). Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported; MRI field strength/software are not shown in this extracted record but missing details do not exclude the study per the criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

The NeuroStore record shows this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cigarette-related videos (I3 satisfied) and reports whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise results with peak tables (I5 and I6 satisfied). However, no analysis in the document is a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (drug cue > neutral) at the same timepoint. Reported contrasts are interactions (e.g., pretreatment crave-resist > posttreatment neutral) or cue > rest regressions, not a simple within-subject drug-cue > neutral-stimulus contrast. Therefore the study lacks the required within-participant cue>control contrast and meets exclusion criterion E5 (between-group/interactions only without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control result).

This study examines alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol (Sauvignon Blanc wine) and control (water) cues and reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol > water) both pre- and post-priming. Analyses were estimated and inference performed at the whole-brain voxelwise level with cluster-based correction and tables of peak coordinates are provided. Participant demographics and clinical details are reported. These features satisfy the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria: visual cue component, within-participant drug-cue>control contrasts, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject contrasts, and is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears accessible via the record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis-related images and matched control images (I3). The paper reports within-participant cannabis>control contrasts for frequent users, sporadic users, and controls (analyses 0–2), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-participant cue>control contrast (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain inference (analyses 0–2: whole-brain corrected cluster probability) and small-volume-corrected results for interactions/regressions, meeting the requirement for whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results (I5). Coordinates/peaks are reported in tables (I6). Participant demographics and preprocessing/statistical model (FMRIB/FSL mixed-effects) and cue type are provided (I7; although field strength is not listed, the guideline allows missing details). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This study uses fMRI with visual appetitive food cues (natural rewards) and reports a within-participant contrast (food > scrambled control images). At least one group-level voxelwise result is reported with whole-brain inference (Analysis 22209236_analysis_0), and coordinate/peak tables are provided. Participant demographics and scanner field strength (3T) are reported. There are no exclusion criteria met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical task fMRI). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study examines cigarette cue reactivity using visual stimuli (2-min smoking video clips vs matched neutral videos), satisfying I3. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing smoking vs neutral videos (interaction immediate > delayed, within-group), satisfying I4. Importantly, it includes group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (analyses with model fit/inference over the whole brain, cluster-corrected), satisfying I5. Voxelwise results are reported as peaks/coordinates, acceptable per I6. Participant age is reported and other missing details do not preclude inclusion per I7. ROI analyses are present but are not the only reported results; no exclusion criteria are met (E3–E6 do not apply). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity and should be INCLUDED.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual stimuli (gambling and smoking pictures). It reports within-participant cue>control contrasts: gambling>neutral and smoking-related>neutral contrast maps used in within-group regression analyses (analyses 10 and 11), indicating within-subject contrasts were computed. Multiple group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain inference and FWE correction (satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting). Results are reported as peaks/tables. Participant demographics and cue types are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI and should be included.

This fMRI study tests visual natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using pictures of high- and low-calorie foods (I3). It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts comparing food categories (e.g., HC>LC and condition interactions water vs glucose) so qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts are available (I4). Analyses were fit and inference performed over the whole brain, and peak coordinates/tables are reported (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results), satisfying the voxelwise evidence requirement (I5). Coordinate results are provided in tables, meeting the allowance for coordinate reporting (I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; some preprocessing/MRI details are not present in this record but missing methodological items do not preclude inclusion per the criteria (I7 not required). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: whole-brain task-evoked results are reported, not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only, and within-subject contrasts are present. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

Excluded because the paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts and does not present a within-participant cue>control contrast. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying within-participant drug-cues>control-stimuli contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (clear visual cue component: silent craving- and aversion-inducing videos), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported with FDR-corrected voxelwise peaks), I6 (results reported as peaks/tables of coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant drug-cues>control-stimuli contrast was reported). Full text is sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study uses a Monetary Incentive Delay Task with visual cues (geometric incentive cues), so it addresses visual reward-related stimuli (meets I3). It reports a group-level voxelwise result with inference restricted to a region of interest (small-volume-corrected) and provides coordinates/peaks (meets I5 and I6). However, the reported analysis is a treatment contrast (bupropion > placebo) during gain anticipation rather than a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., reward-cue > neutral/ control stimulus). The meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant reward-cue>control contrast (I4), which is not present in the NeuroStore extraction. No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are directly triggered; exclusion is based on failing to meet I4. Full text is available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of natural rewards (food) using visual stimuli (images of high- and low-caloric foods) in a within-subject crossover design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of high-caloric > low-caloric food (and the interaction Tea (high>low) – Water (high>low)). Crucially, group-level voxelwise results corrected using small-volume correction (FWE SVC) are reported for predefined ROIs (striatum, OFC, operculum, DLPFC, insula) with peak coordinates in a table. Voxelwise SVC results satisfy the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked group-level statistics. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; missing preprocessing/MRI field-strength details do not preclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI without voxelwise SVC, only connectivity, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This study examines neural responses to visual sexual cues (videos), meeting the review’s focus on natural reward-related visual cue reactivity (I3). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of explicit > exciting stimuli used in group-level analyses (explicit–exciting contrast), satisfying I4. Task-evoked voxelwise results are reported: an ROI small-volume FWE-corrected analysis in the substantia nigra (analysis 0) and voxel-level thresholded associations/contrasts (reported peaks and whole-brain activations in dACC, ventral striatum, amygdala in the abstract), meeting I5 and I6. Participant demographics and cue details are provided, so I7 is met. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI or only connectivity results and includes qualifying task-evoked voxelwise/statistical results. Therefore the study should be included.

This fMRI study examined subliminal visual cocaine cues (visual stimuli, backward-masking) in cocaine-dependent participants. It reports a within-subject contrast of cocaine > neutral cues (analysis 24695721_analysis_2) and group-level voxelwise results: whole-brain inference and cluster-corrected effects for the between-group cocaine>neutral interaction (analyses 5 and 6) with peak coordinates/tables provided. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported. MRI field strength/preprocessing details are not shown in this NeuroStore extract, but I7 is a preferred (not mandatory) reporting item and missing details do not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

The study examines visual alcohol cue reactivity (I3 met) and reports within-participant alcohol>neutral contrasts in ROI-based regressions (I4 met). However, the only voxelwise whole-brain group-level results reported are between-group genotype interaction contrasts (whole-brain two-sample tests); the within-subject alcohol>neutral effects are reported only within ROIs. Therefore there is no qualifying group-level voxelwise within-participant cue>control result required for inclusion. This matches exclusion E5 (only between-group voxelwise contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant voxelwise cue>control). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise within-participant cue>control).

This fMRI study assesses drug cue-reactivity using visual heroin-related pictures versus neutral pictures (meets I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of heroin cues > neutral (within-group LA analysis and within-group results across patients) (meets I4). Analyses were voxelwise, model fit and inference were performed over the whole brain, and peak coordinates/tables are reported (meets I5 and I6). Participant ages and cue type are reported; some other metadata (e.g., MRI field strength) are not shown in this extract but that alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast is present (so E5 does not apply). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study examines neural responses to visual food cues in adults with obesity and reports whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, but it does not report any within-participant contrast of food cues > control (neutral) stimuli. Instead, all reported contrasts compare cognitive-strategy conditions (LATER, DISTRACT, ALLOW) to a NOW condition while viewing the same food images; there is no food-vs-nonfood (cue>control) contrast described. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results), I6 (coordinates/peaks reported), I7 (participant demographics reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control stimuli contrast). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I4.

Excluded because the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) voxelwise analyses where both model fit and inference are restricted to ROIs, violating E3. All reported task-related results are group-by-time-by-stimulus interaction contrasts (between-group/interactions) rather than a simple within-participant cue>control (Food>Object) contrast at group level, so E5 is also met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity to visual food images — a natural reward with clear visual cues). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast reported); I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result — inference was ROI-restricted). Although participant and task details and peak tables are reported, the absence of a qualifying within-subject cue>control and only ROI/inferentially restricted results preclude inclusion.

This fMRI study assesses alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (standardized pictures of alcoholic beverages) in abstinent alcoholics. It reports a within-participant contrast of alcohol-associated > abstract pictures (within-group), with voxelwise model fitting over the whole brain and thresholding that includes whole-volume-corrected and small-volume-corrected results; peak coordinates are reported in Table 3. Although the sample is small (n=6) and the group analysis used a fixed-effects GLM (limiting population generalizability), these do not violate the review’s inclusion criteria. The paper therefore provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results (whole-brain and possibly SVC) for a visual drug-cue contrast and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking images (40 smoking vs 40 neutral) in participants with tobacco use disorder. It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral (one-sample t-test at baseline and a flexible factorial including image type) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise inference and tables of peak coordinates. These features satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (visual drug-cue task), I4 (within-participant drug cues > control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables). I7 (reporting of MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software) is not fully documented in the NeuroStore record (age/sex and cue type are reported), but the guideline states missing one or more of these details alone should not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis images (I3). It reports a within-participant cannabis > non-cannabis contrast (I4). The analysis is a group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked result with whole-brain inference and cluster-corrected thresholding, and reported peak coordinates (I5, I6). Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported; preprocessing/statistical software (FLAME/FSL) and coordinate space (MNI) are listed — MRI field strength is not reported, but this omission is not exclusionary (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical restrictions). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis images with a within-subject cannabis>neutral contrast, but all reported analyses were ROI-based with model fit and inference restricted to an ROI mask (AFNI 3dClustSim cluster correction reported). No whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported. Therefore the study meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual fMRI cue task), I4 (within-participant cannabis>neutral contrast), I7 (participant age/sex and cue type reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/figures to satisfy I5). Consequently the study must be excluded.

The study examines appetitive (happy face) cues (meets I3) and reports group-level voxelwise results including a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis in striatum and whole-brain nogo>go results (meets I5; reporting of results in extracted record acceptable — I6). Participant age/sex are reported (I7). However, no within-participant contrast comparing natural reward-related cues versus control stimuli (e.g., happy > calm) is reported in the extracted analyses. The reported contrasts are response-based (nogo>go) and connectivity (PPI), not a cue>control within-subject contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (no accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Consequently the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that includes clear visual cues (labels/stimuli) and reports a within-participant alcohol>water contrast (Analysis 23876228_analysis_0). That analysis was estimated and inference conducted at the whole-brain level with cluster-based correction and peak coordinates reported (Table), satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. The record also provides participant demographics and cue type. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward-related (high-calorie food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food photographs). It reports a within-subject contrast High-calorie > Neutral pictures (within-group). The analysis was modeled voxelwise over the whole brain with whole-brain inference and correction for multiple comparisons; 18 peak coordinates are reported (Table t1). These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include the required within-participant cue>control contrast. Participant demographics and cues are reported; missing MRI preprocessing details do not preclude inclusion per I7 being preferred but not required. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study examines alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol and soft-drink pictures (cue-reactivity task), and reports group-level voxelwise results. The reported contrast tests the within-participant alcohol>soft drink effect (alcohol vs soft-drink cue blocks) as an interaction comparing AD subgroups (low vs mild/moderate depression), and the model was estimated over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates (p<0.001, cluster extent). Thus it meets: I3 (visual drug cues), I4 (analysis involves the within-participant alcohol>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain result), and I6 (results reported as peaks). No exclusion criteria apply: E3 is not met (not ROI-only), E4 not met (task-evoked contrast present), E5 not met because the between-group interaction is based on the within-subject alcohol>soft-drink contrast. Some methodological details (MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported but I7 is only preferred, and their absence does not preclude inclusion. Full text appears available in the record (no access notice).

Exclusion E5 met: the NeuroStore record reports only a group-by-condition interaction (between-group interaction of metabolizer group x smoking vs neutral) as the whole-brain voxelwise result, but does not report a standalone within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (drug cue-reactivity with clear visual cues — color pictures of smoking vs neutral images), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain result reported, cluster-corrected, peaks listed), I6 (results reported as coordinates/peaks), I7 (participant age/sex and analysis software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no qualifying within-participant drug-cue > control contrast reported in the provided record). Therefore the study must be excluded because it only provides an interaction/between-group contrast without the required within-subject cue>control contrast.

The study reports whole-brain voxelwise results for visual alcohol-related cues (so I3 and I5 are met) and peaks are reported in tables (I6 met). However, all reported contrasts focus on between-group comparisons (AUD vs HC) and the NeuroStore record labels the contrast as "omnibus, between-group." The paper does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., alcohol cues > control) for either group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast).

This study directly assesses alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (standardized alcohol-related pictures) and reports a within-participant contrast of alcohol pictures > neutral pictures (Analysis 17291784_analysis_14) with whole-brain voxelwise results (reported peaks). Additionally, small-volume-corrected ROI associations in ventral striatum are reported (Analyses 4 and 1). Participant demographics and task details are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug cue > control contrast), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result), I6 (reported peaks/tables), and I7 (participant/task reporting). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports a task-evoked fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue reactivity that includes visual stimuli (18 pictures matched to odors). It presents within-participant contrasts comparing high-fat/high-sugar (HFHS) cues versus neutral/ control (NF) cues (HFHS > NF) and interaction contrasts across pre- vs post-surgery sessions, indicating within-subject cue>control effects. Group-level voxelwise analyses were fit over the whole brain and peaks are reported (tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported in this NeuroStore extract (I7 not fully satisfied), reporting omissions do not exclude the study per inclusion rules. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion for the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

The study uses visual monetary reward cues (Euro/cent coins) and tests cue-reactivity in a rewarded task with within-subject contrasts of high-value (Euro) versus low-value (Cent) cues. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results are reported (whole-brain inference, FWE cluster correction, peaks listed in tables). Participant demographics (n, age mean/SD, sex counts) are provided. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues - monetary), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts: Euro>Cent), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results), I6 (coordinates/peaks reported in tables), and I7 (participant info reported; missing MRI field strength does not alone exclude). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

The study reports a whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis of heroin-related > neutral visual cues (Cue Reactivity Task with pictures) and provides reported peak coordinates (Table). The analysis tests differences among A+, A- and HC using the within-participant contrast heroin-related > neutral (model terms include cue condition) and whole-brain inference was performed. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met.

Study examines fMRI responses to appetitive (monetary) conditioning with clear visual cues (colored circles and images of money). It reports within-participant cue contrasts (CS+ > CS−) for controls and patients and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise multivariate PLS results (model fit and inference over whole brain) with coordinate peaks reported. Thus it meets I3 (visual reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (results reported in tables/peaks). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group without within-subject contrasts) apply. Participant demographics and task details are reported; some preprocessing/MRI field-strength details are not extracted here but missing details alone do not exclude the study.

This study investigates neural responses to visual appetizing food cues (natural rewards) using fMRI in healthy participants. It includes within-subject contrasts of food > control (appetizing food vs scrambled/neutral pictures) and reports group-level voxelwise results: a whole-brain second-level contrast (FWE-corrected results, peaks reported) and a region-of-interest analysis with small-volume FWE correction for the amygdala (voxelwise SVC). Participant demographics and MRI field strength (3T) are reported. These elements satisfy the review’s visual cue, within-participant contrast, and qualifying voxelwise result requirements, and results are reported as coordinate peaks. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study assesses cue-reactivity to cocaine using visual stimuli (two 3-minute videotapes of an actor simulating cocaine use), satisfying visual-cue requirement. It reports a within-subject contrast (cue > baseline; cue>control) at the group level (Analysis 16123763_analysis_0 and others), with whole-brain voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates (Talairach), fulfilling the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Coordinate tables/peaks are provided. Participant age/sex and other details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include an appropriate within-participant cue>control contrast. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study tests fMRI responses to visual alcohol-associated cues (I3 satisfied: Naturalistic Movie Viewing with 15 alcohol-associated pictures). The paper reports within-participant cue-induced activation contrasts used in analyses (e.g., cue-induced activation regressed against D2 availability; and the alcohol-associated stimuli > control stimuli interaction), satisfying I4. At least one qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result is reported with small-volume correction/voxel-level correction within regions of interest (inference restricted to ROI; corrected for volume of interest), satisfying I5. Coordinate peaks/tables are reported (I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported (I7 partially met but not required). No exclusion criteria are met: voxelwise small-volume-corrected results are present (so E3 not applicable), task-evoked contrasts are reported (E4/E5 not applicable), and this is empirical fMRI data (E6 not applicable). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

The study reports an event-related fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual heroin-related images and a within-subject drug>neutral contrast (Analysis 25781230_analysis_1) with whole-brain voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates/tables (Table tbl2). Whole-brain model fitting and inference are explicitly stated, and results are reported as coordinates. Participant demographics and analysis software (FILM) are provided. Therefore it fulfills inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked result), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported); I7 (reporting of age/sex and software) is also satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record.

Study is an fMRI RCT of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages). Analyses report alcohol>neutral cue contrasts (cue condition present in models) and task-evoked voxelwise results with small-volume correction (SVC, voxel-level) based on whole-brain model fits. Coordinate/peak results are reported. Participant demographics and cue types are provided. Thus it meets I3 (visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast embedded in reported contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with SVC), I6 (results reported as peaks/coordinates), and I7 (participant age/sex and cue details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue contrasts). Full text appears available via the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study of cigarette cue exposure uses visual first-person videotaped cues and reports within-subject contrasts of cigarette cues > neutral (Analysis 17217932_analysis_0 and related contrasts). Group-level voxelwise results were estimated over the whole brain using FLAME and reported as peak coordinates in tables, with cluster-level multiple-comparisons correction; thus qualifying task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise results are available. The study reports participant age/sex and cue type; MRI field strength is not listed in the extracted record but this omission does not preclude inclusion per review guidance. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue fMRI), I4 (within-participant drug cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (coordinates/tables reporting acceptable) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the provided record.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Specifically, it uses individually tailored audiotaped (auditory) scripts rather than visual cues (I3 not met). The reported task contrasts are group-level between-group comparisons/interactions (e.g., PCE vs NCE for favorite-food vs neutral) and the NeuroStore record does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., favorite-food > neutral) required by I4. The study does include whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (satisfying I5 and I6). Because the paper appears to report only between-group contrasts without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of opioid cue-reactivity using a visual opioid-word Stroop task (meets I3). The paper reports contrasts comparing opioid words to neutral words (opioid>neutral) and defines modulatory change (effective connectivity) and attentional bias based on within-participant opioid vs neutral effects; voxelwise group-level GLM results are reported with 14 peak coordinates (Table tbl0003) and whole-brain inference (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain; FWE cluster-level), satisfying I4 and I5. Coordinate reporting in tables satisfies I6. Although a listed contrast includes a between-group interaction, the abstract and analysis metadata indicate a within-subject opioid vs neutral effect was tested and reported voxelwise. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. fulltext_incomplete set to false.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: (1) It is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using clear visual smoking cues (I3). (2) It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cue > neutral (analyses 0 and 2) (I4). (3) It includes at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked result with whole-brain inference (analysis 2 reports whole-brain FWE-thresholded cluster results and reported peaks), and also small-volume-corrected results (I5). (4) Qualifying voxelwise results are reported in tables/peaks (analysis_2 table t0010) satisfying I6. Participant demographics and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and some preprocessing/software details are not listed but missing details do not preclude inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual smoking images (meets I3). It reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain model fit, thresholding, and 11 reported peaks in Table 1), and results are reported in tables/thresholded maps (meets I5 and I6). However, the NeuroStore extraction does not report any explicit within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., Smoking > Neutral). The only listed contrast is labeled 'Control [simple effect, within-group]', which does not unambiguously represent a smoking>neutral cue contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are explicitly met by the provided record. Exclusion is based on failure to meet I4 (required).

This fMRI study examines appetitive (monetary) Pavlovian conditioning with clear visual cues (2€ coin images and geometric shapes). The NeuroStore record reports within-participant contrasts CS+app > CS− (analysis_2) with group-level voxelwise inference using FWE small-volume correction (voxel-level), satisfying I3 (visual reward-related cue paradigm), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise group result), and I6 (results reported as peaks). The study also includes whole-brain task-evoked analyses and does not rely solely on ROI-only or connectivity-only results, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E5,E6) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study uses visual cannabis cues (pictures of cannabis products/paraphernalia) within a multimodal cue-reactivity task (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of cannabis picture > flower picture and cannabis bimodal > flower bimodal (within-group drug-cue > control-stimulus contrasts), satisfying I4. Analyses were fitted over the whole brain with whole-brain cluster correction and report peak coordinates in tables, meeting the requirement for voxelwise group-level task-evoked results (I5) and allowing coordinate-table reporting (I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; some preprocessing/statistical details (FLAME/FILM) are provided though MRI field strength is not explicitly stated (I7 is not required). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking videos vs control haircut videos). It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking videos > control videos in both stress and non-stress sessions (analyses 19632211_analysis_1 and _2). Results are group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with corrected thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study examined smoking cue reactivity with clear visual cues (42 smoking images, 40 neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM BOLD contrast) and ICA connectivity results. However, the only reported task-evoked voxelwise result is a between-group interaction (slipped > non-slipped for smoking>neutral) rather than a within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli. The other reported analyses are connectivity (ICA) results. Therefore the study does not provide an accompanying within-subject smoking>neutral (drug cue > control) voxelwise result required by the review. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group/interaction reported without within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I5 (at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result reported), and I6 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast reported).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using color photographs (visual cues). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of smoking-related > neutral images (prequit and during abstinence). At least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result is reported with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, cluster-level thresholding, and tables of peak coordinates (Talairach), satisfying the requirement that voxelwise results be available. Results are reported in tables and the main text describes them. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and software are not listed but missing preferred details do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This study uses visual smoking cues and task fMRI, satisfying I3. However, the NeuroStore extraction lists only seed-based gPPI connectivity analyses (whole-brain connectivity) testing a between-group interaction (smokers regulation > ex-smokers craving). No within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus voxelwise task-evoked contrast is reported in the provided document. Therefore the study reports only connectivity/between-group interaction results and lacks a qualifying within-subject cue>control voxelwise result; it meets exclusion criteria E4 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (only between-group/interaction contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 and I5. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study examines visual smoking cue reactivity (16 videos) and reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise smoking > neutral contrast (Analysis 26679479_analysis_0). This provides a within-participant drug-cue > control contrast and a task-evoked voxelwise result suitable for meta-analysis. Participant demographics and cue details are reported. Although the paper also contains ROI and PPI connectivity analyses, these do not exclude the study because a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise cue>control result is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (cocaine and food pictures) (I3). Analysis 31420667_analysis_0 reports a within-participant contrast involving cocaine-related cues versus control (neutral/food baseline) (within-group contrast of Cocaine-Neutral) with reported peak coordinates (I4). The statistical maps were estimated voxelwise over the whole brain and inference used FWE small-volume correction (SVC), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise or SVC-corrected group-level results (I5). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables (I6). Participant demographics and cue type are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI or only connectivity analyses, and includes a qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast, so it is includable.

This fMRI study directly examines alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (NAPS alcoholic and non-alcoholic pictures plus additional images), and reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > non-alcoholic beverage) for the AUD group. Model fitting was performed over the whole brain and coordinates/peaks are reported (Table 3), fulfilling the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Coordinate reporting in tables is acceptable. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported (MRI field strength/software not listed but missing details alone do not exclude). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol stimuli (15 alcohol pictures vs neutral controls) and reports a within-participant contrast (alcohol>control) at the group level. The analysis is voxelwise with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (FWE-corrected results, reported peak coordinates), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Note: MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported in the extracted record, but missing these details alone does not exclude the study (I7 preferred, not mandatory).

This study examines neural responses to visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts of food > blurred baseline, so it meets I3 and I4. However, all reported analyses were fit over a region-of-interest mask (ROI) and no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level task-evoked results are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual stimuli (drug pictures, drug-use tools, drug-use actions, and neutral pictures). It reports a within-subject cue>neutral contrast (drug-related/Drug/Tool/Action > neutral) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain inference (model fit and inference over whole brain; FWE cluster-level thresholding) with peak coordinates reported (Table t3). Participant demographics and cue types are reported. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not listed in the NeuroStore extract, I7 is a preferred reporting item and missing details do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes a within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual drug cue-reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain results.

The study reports a whole-brain task-evoked cue-reactivity between-group contrast using visual food cues (natural rewards), but the NeuroStore record does not present any within-participant cue>control (e.g., HiCal>LoCal or HiCal>neutral) contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cue-reactivity present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result reported), I6 (results reported in tables/peaks), I7 (participant and cue details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no explicit within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (only between-group contrasts for cue reactivity are provided without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Based on the provided document, the study must be excluded.

The NeuroStore extraction indicates that all reported group analyses were restricted to predefined ROIs (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest) for the contrast milkshake receipt > tasteless receipt. This means no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level task-evoked result for visual cue-reactivity is provided. Although the study examines natural reward (food) and includes visual stimuli/food pictures in the experimental paradigm (so inclusion I3 is met) and reports participant demographics (I7 met), it does not report a within-participant visual cue > control contrast relevant to cue-reactivity (I4 not met) and does not provide a whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result (I5 not met). I6 is also not met because no qualifying voxelwise results are available in the extraction. Therefore the study is excluded under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result).

This study reports visual drug-cue (cannabis) fMRI cue-reactivity using photos (I3). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts were estimated over the whole brain and inference used small-volume FWE correction with reported peak coordinates (satisfies small-volume-corrected/voxelwise reporting, I5 and I6). Within-participant cue>control contrasts are present (cannabis>neutral and cannabis>baseline) used in within-group cross-subject regressions and other contrasts, meeting the requirement for a within-participant drug-cue>control contrast (I4). Participant demographics and cue details are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-subject cue>control contrasts. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study reports fMRI of heroin addicts using visual heroin-related videos versus neutral videos. It includes within-participant contrasts of drug video (salient) > neutral video (analyses 0, 3) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain model fit and reported peak coordinates (Tables). Visual cues are clearly used (colour videos). Although some acquisition/preprocessing details are not listed, those omissions do not preclude inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper provides whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (so not only ROIs or only connectivity), and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7.

Excluded because the reported analyses are restricted to ROI-only voxelwise modeling and inference (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) with no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results. This meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task includes visual component: audiovisual smoking-cue and non-smoking cue clips) and I4 (within-participant contrasts SC > non-SC are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3 despite meeting I3 and I4. Full text appears complete for screening (no access issues).

This study reports a task-evoked fMRI whole-brain voxelwise analysis of visually-presented anticipatory cues (Monetary Incentive Delay Task with circle/square/triangle cues), satisfying the visual-cue requirement (I3). The reported contrast is a within-participant interaction comparing cue conditions under nicotine vs placebo (Loss Cue > Neutral Cue within-subject; paired t-test/crossover), which qualifies as a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4). The model was fit and inference conducted over the whole brain with FLAME cluster correction and reported peak coordinates (Table 1), meeting the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results (I5) and allowing coordinate reporting (I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not stated but their absence does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

The study is an fMRI investigation using visual cues (Visual Masking Task with cocaine, neutral, sexual, aversive pictures) addressing drug-related cue-reactivity (I3). It reports a within-group contrast of cocaine > neutral, used in a cross-subject regression predicting affective bias (I4). The model was fit over the whole brain and produced voxelwise group-level results with reported peak coordinates (MNI), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result (I5). Reporting of voxelwise results in the record (reported peaks) satisfies I6. Although the NeuroStore record does not list MRI field strength or preprocessing/software (elements noted in I7 are preferred), the record does provide participant age/sex and cue types; missing those preferred details alone do not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements and is INCLUDED.

The study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, but it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food control). The reported contrasts compare food images with calorie information versus without calorie information, which are experimental condition comparisons within food cues rather than cue>control contrasts required by I4. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study does not satisfy inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded.

This study used visual alcohol cues in an fMRI cue-reactivity task (I3 satisfied). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with coordinates using cluster-corrected inference (I5 satisfied) and provides coordinates/peaks (I6 satisfied). Participant demographics are reported (I7 satisfied). However, all reported statistical results in the NeuroStore record are between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., heavy > light for alcohol > neutral) rather than standalone within-participant cue>control contrasts; the record explicitly labels contrasts as interaction, between-group and lists only between-group contrasts.
