It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie > non-food (Analysis 4: Class III Obesity (HC > NF)) and other HC>NF contrasts, reported as group-level random-effects voxelwise results with whole-brain inference and cluster-level FWE correction (ClusterThresh Monte Carlo). Peak coordinates are reported in tables. Although the NeuroStore record does not list MRI field strength or preprocessing/statistics software, participant age/sex and cue type are reported; missing preprocessing details do not exclude the study per the criteria. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results relating taste reactivity to sweet>neutral tastants and provides coordinate tables (I5 and I6 satisfied). Participant demographics are reported (I7). However, the reported qualifying analyses are gustatory (tastant) contrasts, not visual cue-reactivity contrasts. The extraction lists word cues but the statistical contrasts and reported peaks are for sweet vs. neutral tastants only; no within-participant visual cue (e.g., food picture or word-cue) > control contrast is provided in the document. Therefore the study does not meet the review requirement for a clear visual cue component in a qualifying contrast (I3 not met) nor clearly a within-participant visual cue>control cue-reactivity contrast as required (I4 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the document. Per instructions, the NeuroStore record is treated as the full text.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI responses to visual natural rewards (erotic video clips) in healthy males and includes a within-subject contrast Sexual > Neutral. NeuroStore extraction shows group-level, whole-brain voxelwise model fitting and inference (Talairach space) with thresholding and reported peak coordinates (table), fulfilling the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise result. Visual cues are clearly the stimulus modality. Although details such as MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not reported in this record, the absence of those does not preclude inclusion per the criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-evoked fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural reward) and includes within-participant contrasts of food > non-food for both groups. Voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses are reported with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates in tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This study reports a within-subject visual cue-reactivity contrast (erotic stimuli > neutral stimuli) using event-related fMRI in healthy males, addressing natural reward-related cue reactivity (sexual arousal). The reported analysis is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast (model fit and inference over whole brain) with FDR-corrected voxelwise threshold and reported peak coordinates (Table 2). Although the paper also uses DCM, it provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcoholic and nonalcoholic beverage images). It reports a within-participant contrast ALC>BEV (main effect of ALC-BEV activation) and provides group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, with local maxima reported in a table (Table 3). These elements satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-subject cue>control contrast, and a group-level voxelwise (whole-brain) task-evoked result. Participant and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion E3 met: all reported voxelwise analyses are restricted to regions-of-interest (model fit and inference restricted to ROI/spheres) with no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise cue>control result. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward visual cues: food pictures), I4 (within-participant contrasts of cue condition > control exist, e.g., incongruent > control), I7 (participant age/sex reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). Therefore the study must be excluded because it reports only ROI-limited voxelwise results and lacks the required whole-brain/SVC qualifying results (E3).

The study is a delayed-discounting decision-making fMRI study using chocolate rewards and reports the contrast difficult > easy (decision difficulty). It does not report any within-participant cue-reactivity contrast of natural reward cues > control stimuli (no chocolate-cue > neutral/control contrast), so it fails I4. It is not a cue-reactivity paradigm per se, so I3 is also not satisfied. The paper does include a whole-brain voxelwise analysis (one-sample t-test whole-brain) and reported peak coordinates (satisfying I5 and I6). MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported in the record (I7 not fully satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the required cue>control within-subject contrast for inclusion.

This study uses a Monetary Incentive Delay task with clear visual cues (word cues, targets, feedback) and reports voxelwise small-volume-corrected results (SVC peak-level coordinates), so it meets I3, I5 and I6. However, all reported statistical results in the NeuroStore record are between-group contrasts (comparisons of FHP vs FHN for task phases such as Prospect/Anticipation/Outcome). The record does not present a within-participant cue>control (e.g., reward>neutral) contrast at the group level that would qualify under I4. Per the review criteria, studies that report only between-group contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast must be excluded (E5). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study reports an fMRI task using visual cocaine-related pictures vs neutral pictures and includes a within-participant contrast of cocaine-related > neutral. Analyses were conducted at the whole-brain level with group-level voxelwise statistical results and reported peak coordinates (tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue type, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for visual drug-cue reactivity and should be included.

This study does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast of natural (monetary) reward-related cues versus control stimuli (I4 not met). The report includes visual reward-related cues (slot/stamp machine images) (I3 met) and a group-level voxelwise parametric GLM showing regions correlating with increasing probability of reward (whole-brain, FDR-corrected; I5 met). It also provides coordinate peaks/tables (I6 met). Although it reports a seed-based connectivity analysis, it also reports a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result, so exclusion for connectivity-only studies (E4) does not apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to provide the required within-participant cue>control contrast (I4). Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related cue reactivity using clear visual sexual stimuli), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported as peak coordinates/tables). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 — the reported within-subject contrasts are 'Sex approach > Sex avoid' (approach vs. avoid instruction conditions) rather than a cue>control contrast comparing sexual cues to neutral/control stimuli. Therefore the study does not provide the required within-participant cue>control contrast and must be excluded.

This study assesses visual cue-reactivity using pictures of chocolate vs neutral items (meets I3). It reports within-participant contrasts (chocolate > neutral) for exposure and control groups (meets I4). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise regressions with cluster-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Talairach) in a table (meets I5 and I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and software are not listed but I7 is only a preference and not required. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and within-participant contrasts are present. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record.

The study investigates neural responses to visual sexual stimuli (natural rewards) and reports ROI voxelwise results with small-volume FWE correction and coordinate peaks, but it does not report a within-participant cue>control (VSS>control) contrast. Analyses are parametric modulators of VSS valence/arousal and cross-subject regressions; no explicit VSS>control within-subject contrast is listed. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise results), I6 (results reported as coordinates/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). I7 (preferred reporting items) not fully satisfied (MRI field strength and preprocessing software not reported). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered (e.g., the study did not only report ROI results without small-volume correction). Full text appears complete in the provided record.

The study uses fMRI (MID task) with clear visual cues (arrows, bright flashlight, account balance) assessing natural reward (monetary and verbal) cue-reactivity, satisfying I3. It reports within-participant contrasts of reward>control (vS+ > S- and mS+ > S-), satisfying I4. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with voxel-level FWE small-volume correction (SVC) within the reward-network ROI and peak coordinates are provided in tables, satisfying I5 and I6. Although model fitting was restricted to ROIs, the presence of SVC voxelwise inference meets the meta-analysis requirement for small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Participant sex and cue type are reported, but some preferred details (e.g., full age range, field strength, preprocessing software) are not clearly listed in the NeuroStore record (I7 not applied). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study examines monetary reward cues (MID task) with visual cues and reports small-volume-corrected voxelwise results, meeting inclusion criteria I3, I5, and I6. However, the NeuroStore extraction only reports between-group interaction contrasts (P group > T group for gain anticipation and gain feedback) and does not provide a within-participant cue>control (e.g., gain>neutral) contrast result by itself. This means the paper appears to report only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast, which violates exclusion criterion E5. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Excluded because E5: the paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts (obese BED > obese for HEPF>LEUF / nonfood) and does not report a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related visual cues — food), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported; whole-brain analyses with cluster correction), I6 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). I7 partially met (age/sex and cue type reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing/software not reported).

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visual food cues (images of high-calorie foods vs non-food images) and includes a within-participant contrast (H>O) comparing food cues to control stimuli. The analysis is a group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked result (model fit and inference over whole brain; voxel-level FDR threshold; reported coordinate peaks), satisfying requirements for voxelwise reporting. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. The study thus meets the meta-analysis objective (natural reward visual cue reactivity) and inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes a within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears available from extracted record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses fMRI with a Monetary Incentive Delay task that includes explicit visual cues (nine cue shapes) and monetary reward feedback, satisfying the visual cue requirement. It reports a within-participant contrast of reward-related cue>control (anticipation of monetary gain > neutral), meeting the within-subject cue>control criterion. The gain anticipation result is reported as voxelwise inference with FWE small-volume correction (SVC) with reported peak coordinates (Analysis 1), which satisfies the requirement for at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result. Coordinate peaks/tables are reported (Analyses 1–3), satisfying allowance for coordinate reporting. Participant age and sex and cue-type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue reactivity to natural rewards (monetary).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using personalized visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing visual food cues to written descriptions (Picture > Word; Picture+Word > Word), uses whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses with cluster-level correction and reports peak coordinates, and provides participant demographics. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual food stimuli (high- and low-calorie pictures), addressing natural reward-related cues (food), satisfying the review objective. NeuroStore shows a within-participant task contrast of pictures>baseline (analysis 27866012_analysis_0) reported as a group-level mixed-effects voxelwise GLM with small-volume correction and reported peak coordinates, fulfilling the requirement for a whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked result. Visual cue component is explicit, and results are reported in tables/peaks. Preferred metadata (e.g., MRI field strength/software) are not fully listed in the extraction but missing details do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (only ROI/PPI-only results or lack of within-subject cue>control contrasts) are met. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This fMRI study used visual food cues (natural rewards) in a cue-reactivity task and reports a within-participant contrast of food>non-food (Analysis 24739875_analysis_1) computed as a group-level random-effects GLM with voxelwise whole-brain thresholding and coordinates reported. Thus it provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results. The paradigm, stimuli, and participants are appropriate for natural reward cue-reactivity meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes a within-subject cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant food>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain result), and I6 (voxelwise results reported/available). I7 (preferred reporting details) is partially reported but its absence does not exclude the study. Confidence: 0.88.

The study examines visual food cue-reactivity (natural reward) and reports a task-evoked, small-volume-corrected fMRI result in the posterior fusiform gyrus, but the reported functional contrast is an interaction / between-group comparison (FTO+ Food > FTO− Non-Food). The document does not report a within-participant cue>control (Food > Non-Food) contrast or simple within-subject effect that would qualify for the meta-analysis. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group/interaction contrasts reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cue fMRI), I5 (group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected task-evoked result), I6 (results reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I4. No evidence the full text was unavailable; fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports a visual cue-reactivity task using food images (natural rewards) and includes a within-participant cue>control contrast: Analysis 0 reports a within-group interaction (low-calorie food images post-dosing > placebo versus control images) in a randomized crossover sample. Group-level voxelwise results were fitted and inferred over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates (Tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Coordinate tables are provided. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength is not reported but this omission does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural reward) in an observational cohort of obese adults, using within-subject contrasts (food > non-food and food > blurred baseline) incorporated into group-level random-effects GLMs. Model fitting and inference were conducted over the whole brain, and voxelwise peak coordinates are reported (Tables), with cluster-level correction described (BrainVoyager Monte Carlo). These features satisfy the review requirements for (1) visual cue reactivity to a natural reward, (2) within-participant cue>control contrasts used in group analyses, (3) at least one whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked result, and (4) acceptable reporting of coordinate tables/figures. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and presents qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results for inclusion.

Excluded because the study lacks a visual cue component required by I3: stimuli are gustatory (milkshake vs tasteless) with instructions to hold/swallow, not visual cues. The study does include a within-participant milkshake>tasteless contrast (I4), reports a whole-brain voxelwise analysis with FWE cluster-level inference (I5), and reports peaks in a table (I6). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (professional food photographs). It reports within-subject contrasts of natural reward-related cues > control (high-calorie > control; low-calorie > control) at the group level. Model was fit over the whole brain and voxelwise group-level results are reported (tables of peak coordinates, voxel-level inference p<0.005, cluster extent reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Results are available in tables/figures as required. Participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) and cue type are reported; MRI field strength/preprocessing software not listed but missing details alone do not exclude. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore study meets inclusion criteria.

This fMRI study examines visual sexual (natural reward) cues with within-subject contrasts (preferred > non-preferred; explicit > less-explicit), so it meets I3 (visual natural reward cue) and I4 (within-participant cue>control-style contrasts). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (VOI) models with region-level thresholding and no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results are reported. Therefore it violates I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result). Conclusion: EXCLUDED. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E3. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5.)

The study used visual food cues (meets I3). However, all reported analyses are seed-based task-related connectivity (gPPI) and between-group interactions of regulation conditions; no within-participant cue>control (food>neutral) task-evoked voxelwise contrast is reported. Therefore it fails the required within-subject cue>control contrast and does not provide qualifying task-evoked whole-brain or SVC activation results. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only seed-based connectivity reported without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E5 (reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5 (and I6/I7 not satisfied based on available record). Full text was available for assessment.

This fMRI study examines smokers’ neural responses to smoking cues presented visually (movie scenes) and contrasts smoking scenes with matched control scenes. It used an event-related GLM with a scene condition term (smoking vs control), producing voxelwise second-level random-effects results reported over the whole brain (MNI coordinates; 16 peaks). The reported effects compare smokers versus nonsmokers for the smoking>control contrast, which is based on within-participant cue>control contrasts. Thus the study provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results for a drug (nicotine) visual cue, meeting the meta-analysis objective and required reporting. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (TFCE FWE-corrected peaks) for milkshake > tasteless contrasts, but all reported results are between-group contrasts/interactions (high-risk vs low-risk × milkshake vs tasteless). The record does not document a within-participant cue>control (milkshake>tasteless) contrast reported at the group level independent of the group interaction, nor does it explicitly state a clear visual cue component (only mentions 'milkshake and tasteless cues' without specifying visual presentation). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I6 (results reported in tables/peaks), and I7 (participant age/sex reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no clear evidence of a visual cue component) and I4 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Full text appears available in the record.

Study assesses natural reward (food/beverage) cue-reactivity using written food labels (visual cues). It reports within-subject contrasts of reward cues > neutral (e.g., high-calorie > neutral; low-calorie > neutral) and reward-label comparisons (high- vs low-calorie). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with FWE cluster-level thresholding and tables of peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results. Participant age/sex and cue types are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

Study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (passive viewing of food vs nonfood). It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts of food>nonfood (analyses for restricted and habitual sleep) and a paired t-test interaction (restricted>habitual) using whole-brain model fitting with reported peak coordinates/tables. These satisfy visual cue requirement, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (tables of coordinates). Some secondary details (MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported in this record, but that does not preclude inclusion per criteria. Full text appears available via this NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study does not meet the review’s core inclusion requirements. Exclusion (E5): the paper does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., sucrose>water) — instead reported results are group×condition interactions and cross-subject associations; thus it effectively reports between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-subject cue>control task contrast. Inclusion met: I5 — at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked result appears to be reported within an anatomical ROI with cluster correction (small-volume-style inference); I6 — voxelwise peaks/results are reported. Inclusion not met: I3 — no visual cue component (task used gustatory/tastant stimulation, not visual stimuli); I4 — no within-participant drug/natural reward cue>control contrast is reported. Full text is available in the record (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given failure to meet I3 and I4 and presence of E5, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses visual natural reward cues (food images) and reports within-subject contrasts of food>nonfood (several analyses explicitly labelled ‘food > nonfood’ and omnibus within-group contrasts). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain inference (analyses explicitly list inference over whole brain, cluster-correction details, and reported peak coordinates/tables). Participant demographics and cue types are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This fMRI study used explicit pornographic pictures (clear visual cue component) and tested within-subject contrasts comparing preferred versus non-preferred pornographic stimuli (natural reward-related cue>control-style contrast). Group-level voxelwise analyses were fit over the whole brain, with inference including whole-brain and a ventral striatum small-volume FWE correction; peak coordinates are reported. Participant demographics are provided. These facts satisfy I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast: preferred>non-preferred), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain and small-volume correction reported), I6 (coordinates/results reported), and I7 (participant details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-subject contrasts).

The study reports a visual cue-reactivity fMRI task using food photographs (natural reward cues) and provides a within-participant contrast of food images > objects across all participants. A group-level voxelwise analysis was performed with model fit and inference over the whole brain (FDR-corrected results, reported peak coordinates in Table 2). These elements satisfy the review requirements for (I3) visual natural-reward cue component, (I4) within-participant cue>control contrast, (I5) qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain result, and (I6) reporting of coordinates/peaks. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include a within-subject cue>control contrast). Some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported, but per I7 this alone does not exclude the study.

The study examines natural reward (food) with visual cues (pictures) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results, but the NeuroStore record shows only between-group interaction contrasts (recovered AN > healthy controls for chocolate/strawberry vs controls). There is no explicitly reported within-participant cue>control (e.g., chocolate>tasteless) voxelwise contrast in the document. Inclusion: I3 (natural reward with visual component), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I6 (peaks/tables reported), I7 (participant details present). Exclusion: E5 applies because only between-group/interaction contrasts are provided without an accompanying within-subject cue>control analysis in the record. Therefore exclusion is warranted.

The study used a visual card-guessing (monetary reward) task and reports within-participant contrasts (reward anticipation > baseline; reward outcome > baseline), so it meets I3 (visual natural reward cue) and I4 (within-participant reward>control contrasts). However, all reported analyses are ROI-based with model fit and inference restricted to predefined regions (striatal/prefrontal ROIs); no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results are reported. This violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no qualifying voxelwise result) and means inclusion criterion I5 (at least one qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual food stimuli (images of high-hedonic-value food vs neutral nonfood), with a within-participant contrast (food > nonfood). Group-level voxelwise results are reported within anatomically defined regions of interest, with region-level correction (Bonferroni; p<0.005) and MNI peak coordinates presented in a table (10 peaks per session), which constitutes small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence acceptable under I5/I6. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; details on MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not provided but their absence does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met (not limited to only ROI results without voxelwise peaks, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study examined neural responses to visual food cues (high- vs low-calorie images) in healthy adults and reports voxelwise task-evoked results using small-volume correction within predefined ROIs (mOFC, insula, amygdala). The primary contrast H>L is a within-participant cue-reactivity contrast using visual stimuli. Small-volume-corrected voxelwise peaks are reported, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise or SVC evidence. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without SVC, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study reports fMRI responses to visual food cues and whole-brain voxelwise results (meets I3, I5, I6, I7). However, no within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food > non-food) is reported; analyses are low vs high caloric food and cross-subject regressions with insulin/glucose. Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I4. This violates exclusion criterion E5 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Conclusion: excluded due to E5; inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7; inclusion criteria not met: I4.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (high-calorie food photographs) with a within-participant contrast (high-calorie foods > brick walls). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain inference was performed using SPM5 with multiple-comparisons correction and reported peak coordinates (tables). Participant demographics and software (SPM5) are reported. Although sample size is small (n=3), no exclusion criteria are met and all required inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied.

The study examines natural reward (food) visual cues and includes within-participant dessert>baseline contrasts (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, all reported analyses were fit and inferred within an a priori region-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) with no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results reported. This violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Although peaks are reported in tables, they derive from ROI-restricted analyses, so they do not satisfy the requirement for whole-brain or SVC voxelwise task-evoked results. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

The study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards (food) using visual stimuli (food pictures) and within-participant contrasts (Foods > Objects) under different emotional priming conditions. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and inference was whole-brain FWE-corrected (voxel-level) with peak coordinates reported in tables. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Missing details such as MRI field strength/preprocessing do not preclude inclusion per I7. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This study uses visual food cues (high- vs low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise results, but all reported tests are between-group interactions (sex-by-food) rather than a within-participant cue>control contrast. Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI with visual natural-reward cues), I5 (a qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain result is reported [analysis_2]), I6 (voxel peaks reported in a table), I7 (participant age/sex and cue type reported). Inclusion not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of cue>control reported). Exclusion met: E5 (only between-group/interactions reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

The NeuroStore record indicates fMRI cue-related visual stimuli (drug images and monetary cues), satisfying I3. Analyses were voxelwise but restricted to a striatum ROI (inference restricted to region of interest), which can qualify as small-volume-corrected evidence (I5) and reported peaks (I6). However, all reported statistical contrasts in the document are between-group interactions or group contrasts (e.g., SIB vs SDI, HC vs SDI) rather than a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli (or natural reward > control) contrast. No within-subject cue>control voxelwise contrast is reported in this record. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Excluded for E5. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I4.

The study investigates natural reward (chocolate) cue-reactivity and includes clear visual cues (pictures of chocolate). It reports a within-participant cue>control contrast (choc > tl) with group-level voxelwise results: Analysis 17714197_analysis_0 shows choc > tl with model fit over whole brain and whole-brain multiple-comparisons thresholding; several other analyses report small-volume-corrected results and reported peak coordinates (MNI). Participant characteristics are reported. These satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts).

The study examines alcohol-related visual cues (alcoholic beverage images) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinate tables — satisfying I3, I5, and I6. However, it does not report any within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., alcohol-cue > non-alcohol-cue); reported within-subject contrasts compare emotional valence within cue conditions and the between-group contrasts do not substitute for the required cue>control within-subject contrast. Thus inclusion criterion I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it fails I4 (and therefore does not meet all required inclusion criteria).

This study uses visual erotic photographs (natural reward cues) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results (reported peak tables), so I3, I5, and I6 are satisfied. However, it does not present a clear within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., erotic cue > neutral/resting baseline) reported as a standalone within-subject contrast. Extracted analyses are mainly within-group comparisons of preferred vs nonpreferred sexual cues and between-group interactions that reference resting baseline, but no explicit within-participant cue>control contrast is available in the provided document. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered by the provided document.

This study examines visual food cues (meets I3) but does not report a qualifying within-participant task-evoked voxelwise cue>control contrast. The NeuroStore record shows only (1) ROI-based group analyses (inference restricted to ROI/putamen) and (2) seed-based PPI connectivity results (connectivity, no task-evoked voxelwise thresholded result). All reported between-group/interactions (BE vs non-BE) with no accompanying within-subject high-ED>control whole-brain or small-volume-corrected contrast. Therefore exclusion criteria are met: E3 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task result reported; only ROI/PPI findings), E4 (reports only seed-based connectivity/ROI without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result), and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cues). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no whole-brain or SVC task-evoked voxelwise result). Full text appears complete in this record.

This fMRI study used visual erotic pictures and videos (natural reward cues) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (FWE-corrected coordinate peaks), so it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (peaks reported in tables). However, it does not report any within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli (e.g., erotic > neutral/landscape); the reported contrasts are cue A > cue B (male > female or female > male). Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are triggered. Because I4 is required, the study must be excluded.

The study used visual food cues (pictures) so I3 is met, but the reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based with inference restricted to predefined regions and region-level correction; no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results are reported. In addition, the reported contrasts compare food>money (another reward) rather than food>neutral/control, so the required within-participant cue>control contrast (I4) is not satisfied. Therefore the study is excluded under E3 (ROI-only results).

This fMRI study investigated neural responses to visual food cues (high- and low-calorie images) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE, reported peak tables). It includes within-participant ‘‘food response’’ contrasts used in multiple regression analyses within the EDNOS group (cross-subject regressions of neural food response against OCI and RT), indicating qualifying within-participant cue>control-type contrasts were estimated and tested at the group level. The study therefore meets the review objective (natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cues), I4 (within-participant food-response contrast used in analyses), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported as tables of peaks), and I7 (participant details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, empirical task-evoked data).

The study reports task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity to visual cocaine cues (pictures of cocaine and related objects vs neutral objects) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE cluster-level correction) with reported peak coordinates (tables). The key contrast involves drug cues > control stimuli (cocaine pictures > neutral objects) and is tested in a model including follow-up UDS status (interaction), but the extraction explicitly includes the within-participant cue-type contrast and associated whole-brain peaks. These facts satisfy the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-participant drug>control contrast, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting (peaks in table). Some details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported here, but I7 is only preferred. Slight ambiguity exists because the reported result is an interaction, but the contrast includes cocaine>neutral and is reported as whole-brain peaks, so I include the study.

The study reports a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual heroin-related and neutral images and a within-subject contrast craving>neutral for each group. The model was fit over the whole brain and peak coordinates are reported in tables, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Key inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control contrast), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise result reported), and I6 (results reported in tables) are met. Participant age/sex, cue type, and statistical software/model are reported; MRI field strength is not specified, but reporting of all items in I7 is preferred (not mandatory) and its absence does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study uses visual natural reward cues (appetizing food images) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in tables, but it does not include any within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli. Reported contrasts are choice effects and regulate vs look (reappraisal vs viewing) with no neutral/control stimulus contrast described. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no cue > control within-participant contrast). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-evoked fMRI responses to visual natural reward cues (food images), satisfying I3. It includes a within-participant cue>control contrast (hedonic food cues > non-food objects) reported for an underfed vs eucaloric within-group analysis (OR group), satisfying I4. Results are whole-brain voxelwise group-level statistics (model fit and inference over whole brain, FDR threshold; peaks reported in tables), meeting I5 and I6. Participant age/sex and other demographics are reported, satisfying I7 (preferred details present). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), and a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast is present so E5 does not apply; the paper is empirical human fMRI (not E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study examines valuation of natural rewards (appetitive snack images) with a clear visual cue component (colored backgrounds) and behavioral bidding, meeting the review objective. It contains within-participant contrasts comparing cueON vs cueOFF and parametric modulation by bid size (i.e., within-subject cue>control and value-related contrasts). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with voxel-level FWE small-volume correction (SVC) in predefined ROIs (vmPFC and precuneus) with reported peaks, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results. Voxelwise results are available as reported peaks (NeuroStore entries). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

While this fMRI study of visual food cues meets criteria for natural reward-related visual stimuli (I3), reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain and small-volume correction) and coordinate peaks (I5, I6), and reports participant demographics (I7), it does NOT include a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food cues > control stimuli). The reported analyses are parametric modulations correlating BOLD with inferred pleasantness (association), not a cue versus control contrast required by I4. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are violated. Therefore the study must be excluded because inclusion criterion I4 is not met.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photographs of high- and low-calorie foods). It includes a within-subject contrast (high-calorie > low-calorie) and reports a group-level voxelwise analysis: model fitted over the whole brain with inference restricted to an ROI using FDR small-volume correction (voxelwise SVC result reported). Participant demographics and stimuli are reported. Therefore it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise result with small-volume correction), I6 (results reported appropriately), and I7 (participant and cue details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical task-evoked data present). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study used an event-related Monetary Incentive Delay task with explicit visual cues ($+, $-, 0) probing monetary (natural) reward and loss, and reports within-participant contrasts (reward > no-incentive; loss > no-incentive). Analyses were group-level voxelwise (model fit and inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates (Table), using FSL’s FLAME1 for mixed-effects — satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual reward cue task), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (coordinates reported in table), and I7 (participant/sex variables and software reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical fMRI data). Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used visual food cues (24 food pictures vs 24 visually matched nonfood controls) and reports a within-participant Food>Control contrast. Analyses were group-level mixed-effects (FLAME 1+2) whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with peak coordinates reported in Table t2. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates). Some preprocessing/MRI details are not reported but that does not preclude inclusion per I7 guidance. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) apply. Full text appears available in this record.

This study examines visual food cue reactivity (food images vs blurred control) and reports small-volume-corrected voxelwise ROI results with coordinates and participant demographics. However, the NeuroStore record only shows between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., PWS > OB on food>non-food), and does not report any standalone within-participant cue>control (food>non-food) maps or group-level main effects for the within-subject contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise results), I6 (coordinates reported), I7 (participant age/sex and cue type reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Full text appears complete in the provided record.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-subject contrasts of food > mosaic (control). Group-level voxelwise results were reported over the whole brain (model fit and inference over whole brain) with corrected cluster-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates, meeting the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity.

The study uses visual natural-reward cues (IAPS erotic/affective pictures) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (clusterwise thresholds, reported peak tables). However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts and interaction tests (e.g., ALC erotic > NC neutral; group x gender interactions) and does not present a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., erotic>neutral) as a reported group-level main effect or within-group contrast. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. Full text appears available in the record (no access notice).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (IAPS and commercial photos). It reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie > neutral and other cue>neutral contrasts (I4), and the analyses are whole-brain voxelwise with inference over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (I5, I6). Participant demographics and cue type are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state-only (E4), and include within-participant cue>control contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts (E5). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards and should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without any within-participant cue>control contrast (E5). Met inclusion criteria: I3 (visual erotic stimuli as natural-reward cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked BOLD result reported), I6 (coordinates/peaks reported in table), and I7 (participant demographics reported). Did NOT meet I4: no within-participant drug- or natural reward-cue > control contrast is provided; the functional result described is a between-group interaction (premeno vs postmeno) rather than a within-subject cue>control contrast. Full text appears readable, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports a within-participant contrast of high-GI > low-GI using resting cerebral blood flow (perfusion) with a Rest Task (continuous), not a visual cue-reactivity paradigm. It provides voxelwise whole-brain results but these are not task-evoked visual cue>control contrasts relevant to cue-reactivity. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (resting/perfusion analysis without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise cue-reactivity result). Inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast for drug or natural rewards), and I5 (a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result for cue-reactivity) are not met. Demographics are reported, but cue/stimulus information and task-evoked visual cues are absent, so the study does not meet the review scope.

This fMRI study uses visual erotic stimuli (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected peaks), so it meets I3, I5, and I6. However, it does not include any within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control (e.g., erotic>neutral or erotic>fixation). Reported contrasts are category comparisons (female > male or male > female) rather than cue>control contrasts required by I4. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study examines natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (64 food pictures) satisfying I3. It includes a within-participant contrast of food stimuli > food-neutral images (Analysis 16815041_analysis_0), satisfying I4. The GLM was estimated voxelwise across the whole brain and inference was restricted to a region-of-interest (i.e., small-volume-corrected voxelwise inference), meeting I5. Reported peak coordinates/tables are provided (reported peaks in tables), satisfying I6. Participant age and sex are reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: this is not ROI-only without voxelwise results, nor is it connectivity-only or non-empirical. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements and should be INCLUDED.

This study investigates monetary (natural) reward anticipation using visual cues (shape cues) in an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay task, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results; however, NeuroStore-extracted analyses do not include any within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., reward-cue > neutral-cue). Extracted analyses are interactions/parametric modulations (valence x salience; expected value x salience) rather than a simple cue>control contrast required by inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI of natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked result reported), I6 (voxelwise peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast extracted). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Based on the provided document, the study should be excluded for failing to meet I4.

The study uses visual erotic vs neutral video cues (I3 satisfied) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results with FDR correction (I5 satisfied); NeuroStore extraction indicates voxelwise results are available in tables (I6 satisfied). However, all reported contrasts are treatment-by-condition interaction contrasts comparing erotic>neutral across drugs (e.g., Placebo>Paroxetine, Bupropion>Placebo), i.e., between-treatment interactions, and no simple within-participant cue>control (erotic>neutral) contrast for a single treatment is reported in the extracted analyses. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

The study examines natural reward-related (cola) cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures of logos/bottles). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing strong vs weak brand cues (e.g., Coca/Pepsi > River/T-Cola; Coca Cola > Pepsi Cola), which serve as natural reward-related cue>control contrasts. Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results were estimated over the whole brain (model fit over: whole brain) with reported peaks and MNI coordinates and cluster-level thresholding—satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence. The paper is empirical fMRI (task-based) and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, or between-group contrasts. Some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported in the NeuroStore extract, but I7 is preferred rather than mandatory. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This fMRI study uses visual erotic stimuli (videos and still images) contrasted against control (sport) stimuli, meeting the review focus on natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity. It reports within-subject contrasts of erotic>control (analyses 15961048_analysis_0 and _2) and additional parametric/regression results linked to penile turgidity. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and peaks are reported in tables (Talairach coordinates), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Participant demographics (age, sex, health) and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

The study used a Monetary Incentive Delay task with visual cues (gain vs. neutral), providing within-participant contrasts of natural reward-related cues (gain cues > neutral) for cue anticipation and feedback. Group-level voxelwise results were reported with small-volume familywise error correction (SVC) within anatomically defined ROIs (ventral striatum, mPFC) and peak coordinates are listed (3 peaks per analysis), satisfying the requirement for small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not listed but that missing information alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met (not restricted to ROI-only analyses without SVC; not connectivity/resting-state only; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study reports an event-related fMRI Reward Processing Task using visual symbols indicating possible monetary wins (visual cue component). It includes within-participant paired t-test contrasts of natural reward-related cues versus control (expectation high > no reward; high > low; win > omission), satisfying a cue>control within-subject contrast. Analyses were estimated over the whole brain with group-level random-effects models and report peak coordinates (tables), fulfilling the requirement for a voxelwise whole-brain result (or small-volume-corrected) and allowing coordinate-based extraction. Participant age and sex, cue type, and task details are reported; MRI field strength/software are not listed but these are preferred, not mandatory. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI task data present). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7.

This study reports only ROI-based, cross-subject correlations between BOLD response and free testosterone during viewing of erotic (visual) stimuli in postoperative FtM transsexuals. It does not present a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli, nor any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural-reward erotic cues present), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, and MRI field strength reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5/I6 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC results reported). Therefore the study is excluded.

Study uses visual food cues (pictures of previously tasted functional and standard foods) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts comparing food conditions (first-level food-condition contrasts entered into second-level SPM models). Whole-brain inference reported with coordinate peaks (AlphaSim cluster correction; peaks in tables), satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise result. Although contrasts compare two types of food rather than food vs neutral, this constitutes a within-participant natural reward-related cue contrast (functional vs standard foods) relevant to visual reward cue-reactivity. Seed-based connectivity analyses are also reported but do not preclude inclusion because qualifying task-evoked whole-brain results are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts without a within-subject cue contrast) are met.

The study reports fMRI responses to visual erotic films (natural reward cues), satisfying the review’s cue modality requirement. It includes within-participant contrasts of sexual-cue > rest (M-M > rest in homosexual group; F-M > rest in heterosexual group), meeting the within-subject cue>control criterion. Analyses are group-level, random-effects, voxelwise, whole-brain models with reported peak coordinates (voxelwise thresholding reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Peaks are reported (coordinates), which is acceptable. Participant demographics (age, sex) and task/stimulus details are provided. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

The study reports an event-related monetary (natural reward) task with clear visual cues (numbers and colored feedback). It includes a within-participant contrast of monetary gains > losses (reward-related cues > control) and provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical results (FWE-corrected voxel-level peaks and coordinates) reported in tables. Participant demographics (n, sex, abstinence) are provided. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria for visual reward cue-reactivity (I3), a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), and voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (I5); reporting in tables meets I6, and participant details satisfy I7. The study does not report ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical results, so no exclusion criteria apply. Note: NeuroStore shows a ‘between-group’ tag for the contrast, but the reported model and contrast indicate a within-subject reward>control contrast was tested and reported at the group level.

The study examines neural responses to visual food cues (food photographs) in overweight adolescent girls and reports within-subject contrasts comparing food vs. nonfood stimuli across breakfast conditions. Analyses report voxelwise peak coordinates (tables) from ROI-based voxelwise inference (model fit and inference restricted to predefined ROIs) with cluster-level correction, which constitutes small-volume-corrected, group-level task-evoked results. Thus it meets the review objective for natural reward (food) cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Participant and task details are reported (I7 information preferred but not required). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without SVC, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). The interaction contrasts compare food>nonfood across conditions but are derived from within-participant cue>control effects, so they qualify for inclusion.

This study meets the meta-analysis objectives and inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI task using visual natural reward (food) cues (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast of high-calorie > low-calorie foods (a natural reward-related cue contrast) within groups (I4). The reported results are group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistics with small-volume correction (FWE SVC) within anatomically defined ROIs and peak coordinate tables (I5, I6). Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported; MRI field strength/software are not listed but these are preferred, not required (I7 not fully reported). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI analyses without SVC (E3), is not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), includes within-participant cue>control contrasts (not solely between-group) (E5), and is empirical human fMRI data (not E6). Therefore INCLUDE.

The study uses a Monetary Incentive Delay task with explicit visual cues (green/red/blue squares; star), so it meets I3. NeuroStore reports group-level ROI voxelwise results with FWE cluster correction and reported peak coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. However, the extracted analyses are only between-group contrasts (combined smokers/ex-smokers > controls) for gain and loss anticipation; the document does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g., gain>neutral) at the group level. Therefore it fails I4, and exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete in this record.

This study examines neural responses to visually presented reward cues (card-guessing task with visually presented cards) and reports within-participant task contrasts of reward anticipation/outcome > baseline (analyses 7–10), satisfying the cue>control within-subject requirement. It provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results both whole-brain (analyses 7–10) and ROI-corrected results (analyses 0–6), with reported coordinate peaks and thresholding, meeting the whole-brain / small-volume-corrected reporting requirement. Visual cue component is explicit. Although some preferred metadata (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not listed in the NeuroStore extract, missing these does not exclude the study. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

The study tests visual alcohol-related cues (15 alcohol pictures vs 15 neutral IAPS pictures) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Analysis 22868938_analysis_0 reports a whole-brain, voxel-level FWE-corrected contrast involving alcohol-associated stimuli > neutral stimuli (interaction of cue>control by group), which constitutes a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked cue>control result. Additional analyses include small-volume-corrected task-evoked and PPI connectivity results, but the presence of the whole-brain task-evoked result satisfies the requirement for voxelwise reporting. Participant and task details reported. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, only-connectivity, or only between-group-without-cue contrasts) prevent inclusion. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

Exclusion because the study does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast required by I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward-related visual cues: erotic video clips), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported with corrected voxelwise thresholds), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of sexual cues > control stimuli is reported; analyses are parametric correlational mappings between plethysmographic signal and BOLD rather than a direct cue>control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study reports fMRI reward anticipation using visual cues (grayscale pictures predicting monetary reward), satisfying visual cue requirement. It includes within-participant contrasts of reward-predicting > non-reward-predicting and rewarded > neutral cues (within-group contrasts). Group-level voxelwise analyses were fit over the whole brain with voxel-level thresholding and tables of Talairach coordinates reported, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (coordinates in tables). Participant age/sex are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This study used fMRI with explicit erotic video stimuli (visual cues) and performed within-subject block contrasts between sexually arousing and non-arousing video clips (as stated in the abstract) and a parametric within-group regression with penile turgidity. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise results are reported (Talairach coordinates; cluster-size correction and whole-brain inference are described). Peaks are reported in tables. Therefore it satisfies: I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts performed), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables), and I7 (participant details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears available via the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports visual cue-reactivity to exercise and sedentary images (visual stimuli) and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts (exercise>landscape; sedentary>landscape) at the group level. At least one qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result is reported whole-brain with voxelwise FDR correction (Analyses 24366575_analysis_0 and _1) and coordinates are provided in tables, satisfying the requirement that results be reported as whole-brain voxelwise statistics or in tables. The document provides participant age/sex and cue type; MRI field strength and preprocessing details are not reported in this record but their absence does not preclude inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts without within-participant cue>control contrasts) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study does not assess visual cue-reactivity: the task involves TMS pulses and instructions to recall/imagery of recent drug/alcohol experiences rather than presentation of visual cue stimuli, so I3 is not met. It also does not report any within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli or natural reward-cues > control (no cue>control contrasts are presented), so I4 is not met. The study does meet I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported; whole-brain model fit and peak tables are provided) and I6 (results reported in tables of coordinates). I7 (preferred reporting of age/sex etc.) is partially reported but not essential. No exclusion criteria from E3, E4, E5, or E6 strictly apply. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails required inclusion criteria I3 and I4.

This study uses a Monetary Incentive Delay Task with visual monetary cues (win/lose stimuli), so it meets I3 (natural reward-related visual cues). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates/tables (model fit over whole brain; reported peaks), satisfying I5 and I6. However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts (BEpost-tx vs NBEpost-tx) and does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g., reward-cue > neutral/control) required by I4. Because no qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast is provided, exclusion criterion E5 applies (studies reporting only between-group contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion ID not met: I4. Exclusion applied: E5.

The study examines natural rewards (money and social approval) using clear visual cues (cue symbols and facial expressions), and reports voxelwise small-volume-corrected (SVC) group-level results; however, the NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group interaction contrasts (men>women, women>men) reported at the voxel level. There is no reported within-participant cue>control (or reward>neutral) voxelwise contrast in the extracted analyses; the only within-subject-like analysis is a region-of-interest (right NAcc) ROI analysis. Therefore the study lacks the required within-participant cue>control voxelwise result and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward cue-reactivity with visual cues), I5 (at least one group-level voxelwise result via SVC), I6 (coordinate reporting acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast).

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level task contrasts (food>baseline) presented in tables, so it satisfies I3, I5, and I6. However, all reported statistical results in the NeuroStore record are between-group interaction contrasts comparing genetic subtypes (DEL vs UPD) for Food>Baseline; the record does not present a within-participant cue>control (e.g., food>baseline) contrast for a single group. Because the paper reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast, it violates exclusion criterion E5 and fails inclusion criterion I4. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study examines visual food cue reactivity (high- vs low-caloric food and non-food pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts (food>non-food), so it meets I3 and I4, and reports voxel peaks in a table (I6). However, the reported voxelwise whole-brain result (Analysis 2) is from a single participant using a fixed-effect single-arm design (n=1). Inclusion criterion I5 requires at least one qualifying analysis to be a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result (whole-brain or SVC). Because all analyses are single-subject/fixed-effect (not group-level), the study does not satisfy I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) strictly apply, but failure to meet I5 mandates exclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (group-level voxelwise result). Full text is complete as provided.

The study is excluded because it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (required I4). The reported analyses are parametric modulations of valence/willingness ratings during presentation of food pictures, not explicit food>neutral or cue>control contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward-related visual cues — food pictures), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results reported with peak coordinates), I6 (results reported in tables/coordinates acceptable). I7 (reporting of participant age/sex and cue type present; MRI field strength/software not reported) is not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria (I4 missing) and is excluded.

This study reports only resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity analyses (ACC-seeded rsFC) with no task or cue presentation (task listed as Rest, eyes closed). It therefore does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues (I3 not met), contains no within-participant cue>control task contrast (I4 not met), and provides no task-evoked voxelwise results (I5/I6 not met). It also does not fully satisfy reporting preferences in I7 (some participant info present but cue type/MRI field strength/preprocessing details are not reported). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only seed-based/resting-state analyses with no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result).

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports voxelwise small-volume-corrected results (reported peaks), but it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli (e.g., food images > neutral/control images). Included criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise SVC results), I6 (coordinate table peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported); I7 (MRI field-strength and preprocessing/statistical software not reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I4.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 and E5. The NeuroStore record reports only resting-state rs-fMRI analyses (global connectedness) and a between-group interaction (STIM vs SHAM) of change from Day 1 to Day 2, with no task-evoked cue-reactivity results. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant age/sex reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no clear visual cue component — cues are Pavlovian cues linked to food odors, not clearly visual), I4 (no within-participant cue>control task contrast for drug or natural reward cues), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked result; only resting-state voxelwise maps). Therefore the study does not meet the review requirement for task-evoked visual cue-reactivity and must be excluded.

The NeuroStore record does not provide a within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast for natural reward stimuli (e.g., sexual>neutral or infant>neutral). The only extracted voxelwise group analysis is 'negative > fixation' (whole-brain, FDR-corrected), which does not qualify as a natural reward cue>control contrast. Although the abstract describes VTA increases to crying infant and sexual images after oxytocin, no qualifying voxelwise cue>control result (whole-brain or SVC) for those stimulus types is presented in the provided document. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues present) and I5 (group-level voxelwise result reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no qualifying cue>control contrast reported); I6 (no clear indication in this document that qualifying voxelwise cue>control results are available in tables/figures/supplementary). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

The study uses visual erotic IAPS pictures (natural reward-related cues) and reports within-participant contrasts including erotic pictures versus baseline and parametric within-group contrasts comparing erotic vs non-erotic self-relatedness. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (voxel-level threshold p<0.001, cluster extent 10) with peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards (palatable food images) using a visual task and within-subject contrasts (palatable foods > neutral items). NeuroStore shows group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with FWE thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Results are reported in tables of coordinates. While some preferred metadata (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not shown in this record, missing those details alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the paper meets inclusion I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study examines neural responses to sweet taste with visual predictive cues (meets I3). It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume FWE correction (meets I5) and publishes coordinate tables/peaks (meets I6). Participant age and sex and cue type are reported (meets I7).
